## Calculated Values {#sec-calculated}

Parameters derived from mathematical formulas and economic models.

### Annual Funding from 1% of Global Military Spending Redirected to DIH: $27.2B {#sec-treaty_annual_funding}

::: {.callout-note collapse="true" title="📊 Details"}

Annual funding from 1% of global military spending redirected to DIH

**Inputs**:

- [Global Military Spending in 2024](#sec-global_military_spending_annual_2024) 📊: $2.72T
- [1% Reduction in Military Spending/War Costs from Treaty](#sec-treaty_reduction_pct): 1%

$$
\begin{gathered}
Funding_{treaty} \\
= Spending_{mil} \times Reduce_{treaty} \\
= \$2.72T \times 1\% \\
= \$27.2B
\end{gathered}
$$

*✓ High confidence*

:::

### US Efficiency Rating: 38.8% {#sec-us_gov_efficiency_rating}

::: {.callout-note collapse="true" title="📊 Details"}

US federal spending efficiency rating. Complement of waste percentage. Measures what fraction of fiscal input converts to useful output. Compare to OECD benchmark of 75-85%.

**Inputs**:

- [US Government Waste (Total)](#sec-us_gov_waste_total) 🔢: $4.16T
- [US Federal Spending (FY2024)](#sec-us_federal_spending_2024) 📊: $6.80T

$$
\begin{gathered}
E_{US} = 1 - \frac{W_{total,US}}{Spending_{federal}} = 1 - \frac{\$4.16T}{\$6.8T} = 38.8\% \\[0.5em]
\text{where } W_{total,US} = W_{raw,US} \times US = \$4.9T \times 0.85 = \$4.16T \\[0.5em]
\text{where } W_{raw,US} \\
= W_{health} + W_{housing} + W_{military} \\
+ W_{regulatory} + W_{tax} + W_{corporate} \\
+ W_{tariffs} + W_{drugs} + W_{fossil} \\
+ W_{agriculture} \\
= \$1.2T + \$1.4T + \$615B + \$580B + \$546B \\
+ \$181B + \$160B + \$90B + \$50B + \$75B \\
= \$4.9T
\end{gathered}
$$

*~ Medium confidence*

#### Sensitivity Analysis

### US Waste (% GDP): 14.5% {#sec-us_gov_waste_pct_gdp}

::: {.callout-note collapse="true" title="📊 Details"}

US government waste as percentage of GDP. ~$4.15T waste / $28.78T GDP = ~14%. This represents the 'dysfunction tax' that American citizens effectively pay through inefficient governance.

**Inputs**:

- [US Government Waste (Total)](#sec-us_gov_waste_total) 🔢: $4.16T
- [US GDP (2024)](#sec-us_gdp_2024) 📊: $28.8T

$$
\begin{gathered}
W_{US,\%GDP} = \frac{W_{total,US}}{USGDP} = \frac{\$4.16T}{\$28.8T} = 14.5\% \\[0.5em]
\text{where } W_{total,US} = W_{raw,US} \times US = \$4.9T \times 0.85 = \$4.16T \\[0.5em]
\text{where } W_{raw,US} \\
= W_{health} + W_{housing} + W_{military} \\
+ W_{regulatory} + W_{tax} + W_{corporate} \\
+ W_{tariffs} + W_{drugs} + W_{fossil} \\
+ W_{agriculture} \\
= \$1.2T + \$1.4T + \$615B + \$580B + \$546B \\
+ \$181B + \$160B + \$90B + \$50B + \$75B \\
= \$4.9T
\end{gathered}
$$

*~ Medium confidence*

### Recoverable Capital: $2.08T {#sec-us_gov_waste_recoverable}

::: {.callout-note collapse="true" title="📊 Details"}

Recoverable capital if US improved to OECD median efficiency. Current US efficiency ~38-48%; OECD median ~75-85%. Closing to ~80% would recover approximately half the gap.

**Inputs**:

- [US Government Waste (Total)](#sec-us_gov_waste_total) 🔢: $4.16T

$$
\begin{gathered}
W_{US,recoverable} \\
= W_{total,US} \times 0.5 \\
= \$4.16T \times 0.5 \\
= \$2.08T \\[0.5em]
\text{where } W_{total,US} = W_{raw,US} \times US = \$4.9T \times 0.85 = \$4.16T \\[0.5em]
\text{where } W_{raw,US} \\
= W_{health} + W_{housing} + W_{military} \\
+ W_{regulatory} + W_{tax} + W_{corporate} \\
+ W_{tariffs} + W_{drugs} + W_{fossil} \\
+ W_{agriculture} \\
= \$1.2T + \$1.4T + \$615B + \$580B + \$546B \\
+ \$181B + \$160B + \$90B + \$50B + \$75B \\
= \$4.9T
\end{gathered}
$$

### Efficiency Gap / Treaty Funding: 153:1 {#sec-us_gov_waste_vs_treaty_multiplier}

::: {.callout-note collapse="true" title="📊 Details"}

How many times the US government efficiency gap could fund the 1% Treaty. The efficiency gap represents capital that could fund transformative health research many times over.

**Inputs**:

- [US Government Waste (Total)](#sec-us_gov_waste_total) 🔢: $4.16T
- [Annual Funding from 1% of Global Military Spending Redirected to DIH](#sec-treaty_annual_funding) 🔢: $27.2B

$$
\begin{gathered}
k_{waste:treaty} = \frac{W_{total,US}}{Funding_{treaty}} = \frac{\$4.16T}{\$27.2B} = 153 \\[0.5em]
\text{where } W_{total,US} = W_{raw,US} \times US = \$4.9T \times 0.85 = \$4.16T \\[0.5em]
\text{where } W_{raw,US} \\
= W_{health} + W_{housing} + W_{military} \\
+ W_{regulatory} + W_{tax} + W_{corporate} \\
+ W_{tariffs} + W_{drugs} + W_{fossil} \\
+ W_{agriculture} \\
= \$1.2T + \$1.4T + \$615B + \$580B + \$546B \\
+ \$181B + \$160B + \$90B + \$50B + \$75B \\
= \$4.9T \\[0.5em]
\text{where } Funding_{treaty} \\
= Spending_{mil} \times Reduce_{treaty} \\
= \$2.72T \times 1\% \\
= \$27.2B
\end{gathered}
$$

*~ Medium confidence*

#### Sensitivity Analysis

### Agricultural Subsidies Deadweight Loss: $75B {#sec-us_gov_waste_agricultural_subsidies}

::: {.callout-note collapse="true" title="📊 Details"}

Deadweight loss from US agricultural subsidies. Direct subsidies ~$30B/yr but create larger distortions: overproduction, environmental damage, benefits concentrated in large farms (top 10% receive 78% of subsidies). Total welfare loss ~$75B. Textbook example of capture; very high economist consensus.

**Source**: [@ewg-farm-subsidies]

#### Uncertainty Range

**Technical**: 95% CI: [$50B, $120B] • Distribution: Lognormal (SE: $25B)

**What this means**: There's significant uncertainty here. The true value likely falls between $50B and $120B (±47%). This represents a wide range that our Monte Carlo simulations account for when calculating overall uncertainty in the results.

*The lognormal distribution means values can't go negative and have a longer tail toward higher values (common for costs and populations).*

#### Input Distribution

{{< include ../figures/distribution-us_gov_waste_agricultural_subsidies.qmd >}}

*✓ High confidence*

:::

### Corporate Welfare Waste: $181B {#sec-us_gov_waste_corporate_welfare}

::: {.callout-note collapse="true" title="📊 Details"}

Direct US federal corporate welfare: subsidies to agriculture ($16.4B), green energy tax credits, semiconductor aid, aviation support. Agricultural subsidies are highly regressive (top 10% receive 63%). Cato Institute forensic tally.

::: {.callout-note collapse="true" title="📊 Details"}

US healthcare spending inefficiency. US spends ~$4.5T/yr (18% GDP) vs 9-11% in comparable OECD countries with similar/better outcomes. Papanicolas et al. ### Housing/Zoning Restrictions Cost: $1.40T {#sec-us_gov_waste_housing_zoning}

::: {.callout-note collapse="true" title="📊 Details"}

GDP loss from housing/zoning restrictions. Hsieh & Moretti (2019 AEJ:Macro) estimate restrictive zoning in high-productivity cities (NYC, SF, Boston) lowered aggregate US GDP by 36% from 1964-2009 by preventing workers from moving to productive locations. Annual cost ~$1.4T. Very high economist consensus across political spectrum.

**Source**: [@hsieh-moretti2019]

#### Uncertainty Range

**Technical**: 95% CI: [$1T, $2T] • Distribution: Lognormal (SE: $300B)

**What this means**: There's significant uncertainty here. The true value likely falls between $1T and $2T (±36%). This represents a wide range that our Monte Carlo simulations account for when calculating overall uncertainty in the results.

*The lognormal distribution means values can't go negative and have a longer tail toward higher values (common for costs and populations).*

#### Input Distribution

{{< include ../figures/distribution-us_gov_waste_housing_zoning.qmd >}}

*✓ High confidence*

:::

### Military Overspend: $615B {#sec-us_gov_waste_military_overspend}

::: {.callout-note collapse="true" title="📊 Details"}

US military spending above 'Strict Deterrence' baseline. Current budget ~$900B supports global power projection (750+ bases). Strict Deterrence (nuclear triad $95B, Coast Guard $14B, National Guard $33B, Missile Defense $28B, Cyber $15B, defensive Navy/Air Force $100B) = ~$285B. Delta: $900B - $285B = $615B 'Hegemony Tax'.

**Source**: [@political-dysfunction-tax-paper-2025]

#### Uncertainty Range

**Technical**: 95% CI: [$500B, $750B] • Distribution: Normal (SE: $75B)

**What this means**: This estimate has moderate uncertainty. The true value likely falls between $500B and $750B (±20%). This represents a reasonable range that our Monte Carlo simulations account for when calculating overall uncertainty in the results.

*The normal distribution means values cluster around the center with equal chances of being higher or lower.*

#### Input Distribution

{{< include ../figures/distribution-us_gov_waste_military_overspend.qmd >}}

*~ Medium confidence*

:::

### Regulatory Red Tape Waste: $580B {#sec-us_gov_waste_regulatory_red_tape}

::: {.callout-note collapse="true" title="📊 Details"}

Deadweight loss from US regulatory red tape (procedural friction without safety benefits). Competitive Enterprise Institute estimates total regulatory burden at $2.15T; European studies find red tape costs 0.1-4% of GDP. Conservative estimate: ~2% of US GDP = $580B.

**Source**: [@political-dysfunction-tax-paper-2025]

#### Uncertainty Range

**Technical**: 95% CI: [$290B, $1T] • Distribution: Lognormal (SE: $200B)

**What this means**: This estimate is highly uncertain. The true value likely falls between $290B and $1T (±61%). This represents a very wide range that our Monte Carlo simulations account for when calculating overall uncertainty in the results.

*The lognormal distribution means values can't go negative and have a longer tail toward higher values (common for costs and populations).*

#### Input Distribution

:::

### Tariff Cost (GDP Loss): $160B {#sec-us_gov_waste_tariffs}

::: {.callout-note collapse="true" title="📊 Details"}

Annual GDP reduction from US tariffs and retaliation. Yale Budget Lab estimates 0.6% smaller GDP in long run, equivalent to $160B annually. Trade barriers reduce efficiency and raise consumer prices.

**Source**: [@yalebudgetlab2025]

#### Uncertainty Range

**Technical**: 95% CI: [$90B, $250B] • Distribution: Normal (SE: $50B)

**What this means**: There's significant uncertainty here. The true value likely falls between $90B and $250B (±50%). This represents a wide range that our Monte Carlo simulations account for when calculating overall uncertainty in the results.

*The normal distribution means values cluster around the center with equal chances of being higher or lower.*

### Tax Compliance Waste: $546B {#sec-us_gov_waste_tax_compliance}

::: {.callout-note collapse="true" title="📊 Details"}

Annual cost of US tax code compliance: 7.9 billion hours of lost productivity ($413B) plus $133B in out-of-pocket costs. Equals nearly 2% of GDP. Could be largely eliminated with simplified tax code or return-free filing.

**Source**: [@taxfoundation2024-compliance]

#### Uncertainty Range

**Technical**: 95% CI: [$450B, $650B] • Distribution: Normal (SE: $50B)

**What this means**: This estimate has moderate uncertainty. The true value likely falls between $450B and $650B (±18%). This represents a reasonable range that our Monte Carlo simulations account for when calculating overall uncertainty in the results.

*The normal distribution means values cluster around the center with equal chances of being higher or lower.*

```{=html}
<script>
// Conservative lazy loading: only load images actually in viewport
(function() {
  'use strict';
  
  let imageObserver = null;
  let loadTimeout = null;
  
  function enableLazyLoading() {
    const images = document.querySelectorAll('img');
    
    // Use Intersection Observer with conservative threshold
    // rootMargin: '50px' means only load images within 50px of viewport
    // This prevents loading images passed through during hash navigation
    imageObserver = new IntersectionObserver((entries, observer) => {
      entries.forEach(entry => {
        if (entry.isIntersecting && entry.intersectionRatio > 0) {
          const img = entry.target;
          // Only load if image is actually visible (not just passed through)
          if (img.dataset.src) {
            img.src = img.dataset.src;
            img.removeAttribute('data-src');
          } else if (!img.hasAttribute('loading')) {
            // For images without data-src, use native lazy loading
            img.setAttribute('loading', 'lazy');
          }
          observer.unobserve(img);
        }
      });
    }, {
      rootMargin: '50px',  // Only load images within 50px of viewport
      threshold: 0.01      // Trigger when at least 1% visible
    });
    
    images.forEach(img => {
      imageObserver.observe(img);
    });
  }
  
  // Handle hash navigation (clicking links to sections)
  // Delay loading to avoid loading images passed through during jump
  function handleHashNavigation() {
    if (loadTimeout) clearTimeout(loadTimeout);
    // Wait 300ms after navigation to let scroll settle
    // Images will load naturally via Intersection Observer when visible
    loadTimeout = setTimeout(() => {
      // Scroll has settled, Intersection Observer will handle visible images
      // No action needed - observer is already watching
    }, 300);
  }
  
  // Initialize on page load
  if (document.readyState === 'loading') {
    document.addEventListener('DOMContentLoaded', enableLazyLoading);
  } else {
    enableLazyLoading();
  }
  
  // Handle hash changes (clicking anchor links)
  window.addEventListener('hashchange', handleHashNavigation);
  
  // Also handle initial hash if page loads with one
  if (window.location.hash) {
    setTimeout(handleHashNavigation, 100);
  }
})();
</script>
```
